subject: Thermal headroom & affinity sweep for NeoEdge late-stage commitment
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Simms <laura.simms@neoedge.ai>
Cc: procurement@neoedge.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Thermal headroom & affinity sweep for NeoEdge late-stage commitment

Team — looping you all in on a late-stage ask from NeoEdge (deal NEO-7421). They want a Dedicated pool sizing confirmation and an internal validation that we have the thermal/affinity headroom to sustain a 24/7 inference SLA at p95 for the requested workload. High level: they expect sustained 2k tokens/sec for their production model (~70B) with peak bursts to 3.5k tokens/sec. They plan to commit to a 12-month reserved capacity if we can certify availability and a soft-hold this month.

Key asks from NeoEdge (copied):
- Confirm node-level affinity mapping (can we reserve contiguous A100 slices / 8xA100 equivalent)
- Thermal headroom at p95 over 30d window (we should show >=30% spare thermal capacity for continuous inference)
- Fallback plan: if full-precision capacity constrained, ability to switch to 8-bit quantized variant with <1.5x latency increase

Attachments: I attached their affinity matrix (neoedge_affinity_map_v2.csv) and their initial workload profile.

Dev/Marcus — can you run an internal sweep across us-west-2 pool for the requested run-rate and return:
1) a node mapping proposal (which node groups we would pin)
2) a thermal/power headroom summary with p50/p95 numbers over our last 30-day telemetry for those nodes
3) whether continuous 24/7 at the requested token/sec is feasible without eviction risk

Marissa/Karthik — can you confirm commercial runway (they've asked for a soft-hold through EOD 2026-10-18) and whether this triggers a dedicated SLA review?

Target: internal validation + soft-hold decision by 2026-10-15 so we can get procurement/PO moving.

Thanks — Jonas
Jonas Weber
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai
+1-415-555-0199

Attachments referenced: neoedge_affinity_map_v2.csv (CSV, 42KB), workload_profile_neoedge.xlsx (XLSX, 36KB)
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Simms <laura.simms@neoedge.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Thermal headroom & affinity sweep for NeoEdge late-stage commitment

Jonas / team — quick update from infra after an initial pass.

Summary (short): feasible with caveats. We can map NeoEdge to 10 dedicated nodes (8xA100-equivalent slices per node), but to meet sustained 2k tokens/sec with p95 latency SLO we'll need:
- a hard pin of contiguous physical GPUs (to avoid cross-tenant thermal interference)
- enabling aggressive prefix caching (saves ~18% token work for their typical prompt distribution)

Thermal headroom (prelim):
- For the candidate node group in us-west-2 (cluster-west-3): p50 spare thermal capacity = 43%, p95 = 28% over the last 30 days.
- p95 is slightly under the 30% target Jonas asked for — that 28% shortfall is driven by two recent heavy-training jobs last month that spiked rack temps.

Mitigations/options:
1) Rebalance a subset of training jobs away from cluster-west-3 (ops availability window needed) — expected to raise p95 headroom to ~33% within 72 hours.
2) Offer a hybrid: 8 dedicated nodes plus 2 overflow nodes with auto-fallback to quantized weights for burst windows. Overflow fallback reduces headroom pressure but adds 10–15% latency on bursts.
3) Approve temporary node throttling (lower clock/freq) to increase headroom — would increase baseline latency by ~7% but keep full-precision.

Action items I can run if you want:
- Full telemetry sweep and heatmap by rack for the nodes we propose (I can deliver CSV + PDF) — ETA 18 hrs.
- Stand up the soft-hold in cluster scheduling to reserve the contiguous slices (requires approvals from Marcus for a 7-day scheduler exception).

I'll attach the thermal headroom extract (thermal_headroom_q3_2026.pdf) and a tentative node mapping CSV once I run the sweep.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.ai
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Simms <laura.simms@neoedge.ai>, procurement@neoedge.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Thermal headroom & affinity sweep for NeoEdge late-stage commitment

Thanks Dev — that summary is super helpful. A couple clarifications:

- The 30% p95 is a hard ask from their infra/security team for continuous inference. If we can get p95 >> 30% after rebalancing (option 1), that should unlock the 12-month reserved commitment.
- Marissa: please confirm whether we can offer a 7-day soft-hold on contiguous slices while we do the rebalance. The customer is sensitive to any visible degradation, so if we need to do the rebalance with a maintenance window we should propose an EOD low-impact window and give them an ETA.

Dev / Marcus — please proceed with the full telemetry sweep and heatmap. Deliverables requested: node mapping CSV, rack-level thermal heatmap (PDF), and a short runbook showing operational steps to do the rebalance (including expected downtime/maintenance window). ETA for deliverables: EOD 2026-10-13.

I'll update NeoEdge with a proposed soft-hold and the tentative timeline. If you see any blocker that prevents the 7-day scheduler exception, flag it immediately.

Jonas

Appreciate the quick turnaround everyone. From the commercial side:

- We can offer NeoEdge a 7-day soft-hold for the contiguous slices starting 2026-10-15 pending the telemetry deliverables. That soft-hold will not be billable until they sign the 12-month reserved contract; it's purely a scheduler reservation and requires Marcus' approval for the scheduler exception.
- Karthik and I will prepare a conditional term addendum to the SOW that ties availability to the thermal headroom remediation. If Dev/Marcus can show p95 >= 30% after rebalancing (or the hybrid plan with overflow auto-fallback), we'll mark the hard commitment green and prep the PO language.
- Procurement (NeoEdge): if you can send a preliminary PO or an intent-to-sign note, we can prioritize the rebalance window and lock the soft-hold.

Marcus — please confirm scheduler exception approval and any operational notes we should tell NeoEdge about (maintenance windows, expected outage windows if any).

I'll draft a short customer-facing note once we have the heatmap and node mapping.

— Marissa
